name: QFQ Packet Scheduler Module Not Loaded
description:
Ensures the QFQ (Quick Fair Queueing) traffic control scheduler module sch_qfq is not loaded (checked in /proc/modules). sch_qfq has a history of use-after-free flaws that a local user can use for privilege escalation, most recently CVE-2026-99688 (CVSS 7.8), and earlier CVE-2023-4921 and CVE-2025-38477; where unprivileged user namespaces are allowed, any local user can configure qdiscs and load the module. Red Hat recommends blocking the module as a mitigation: add 'install sch_qfq /bin/true' to a file in /etc/modprobe.d. A driver compiled into the kernel is not detected. Hosts whose traffic shaping uses QFQ fail; exclude them and install the patched kernel from the vendor errata.
Required sudo rule (remedy only): allow user lea to run ONLY this exact command without a password: lea ALL=(root) NOPASSWD: /sbin/modprobe -r sch_qfq
